executive_assessment.text: Eight named provinces have dated August 2026 vegetation concerns, while southern and Lac farming also faced separately reported insecurity constraints.
N'Djamena's reported drainage, pumping and preparedness outputs add concrete capacity. Historical flood and access findings are not combined into an unsupported causal chain.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2026-09-07 reports: FAO’s 7 September 2026 brief reports that erratic rains and dry spells left poor satellite vegetation conditions by mid-August in Logone Occidental, Logone Oriental, Mandoul, Moyen-Chari, Lac, Batha, Wadi Fira and Ouaddaï.

Source dated 2026-09-07 reports: FAO estimated 2025 cereal output at 3 million tonnes, 10% above its five-year average, but reported lower output in parts of the Sudanian zone and localized shortfalls where civil insecurity disrupted farming in Lac and southern areas.

Source dated 2026-05-26 reports: The World Bank says N’Djamena, at the Chari–Logone confluence, faces high flood risk from intense rains, rapid urban growth, clogged drains and limited emergency capacity; risk heightened after the 2022 floods and ahead of the 2024 rainy season.

Source dated 2026-05-26 reports: The World Bank reports that 2024 PILIER works cleared and repaired 350 km of N’Djamena drains, deployed 12 pumps, trained about 30 technicians, and provided neighborhood maps and pre-positioned supplies benefiting 9,858 households; the city remained largely unharmed during high river levels.
Source dated 2026-02-09 reports: UNICEF reports 2025 floods killed people and displaced residents in Mandoul, Moyen-Chari, Salamat and Wadi Fira; the season was milder than 2022 and 2024.

Source dated 2026-02-09 reports: Citing OCHA, UNICEF says access restrictions prevented assessment or aid during displacement events in Logone Occidental, Ouaddaï and Mayo Kebbi Ouest; armed groups remained active on Lake Chad islands.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 11 of 16 evidence records and 0 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The Eastern Chad climate-security assessment could not be opened from either UN publisher route, so this extraction does not include its country-specific eastern-region climate-conflict findings.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
Modeled present-day 100-year flood exposure is not an observed affected-person count.
No inspected source establishes a climate-to-violence causal pathway in Chad; co-occurrence of climate hazards, insecurity and displacement is not treated as causation.
FAO's September 2026 crop brief is a dated seasonal snapshot; its 2026 outlook was not treated as a verified final harvest result.

UNICEF's 2025 flood paragraph provides named provinces but no household-level loss estimates; its access restrictions are cited from an OCHA overview and relate to displacement events not linked to flooding.
The World Bank's N’Djamena results brief attributes preparedness outcomes to PILIER but gives no independent counterfactual estimate of losses avoided.
The March 2026 Lake Chad research PDF timed out and the IOM May 2026 DTM page returned 403; no findings from their search excerpts were used.
Main checked the original FAO, UNICEF and World Bank passages. The N'Djamena results concern 2024 preparedness, not all Chad flood losses.
SPARC findings are not reused in this draft, pending a separate reuse-terms check. No general legal conclusion about paraphrase rights is made.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.

The floodplain displacement mechanism is documented at report level. Eastern Chad, Lac and N'Djamena require separate project-location verification; evidence from one does not establish another's mechanism.
